basic_identification.full_title: Automotive Vehicles — Electric Horns — Specification (Third Revision)
basic_identification.sector_category: Transport Engineering / Automotive Electrical Equipment (approved by the Transport Engineering Division Council and finalized by the Automotive Electrical Equipment Sectional Committee of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

scope.summary: This standard specifies the mechanical, electrical, and acoustical requirements, as well as methods of tests for 6 V, 12 V, 24 V, and 48 V electric horns for use in motor vehicles, including those intended for two and three wheelers.
scope.page_number: Page 1 of base standard / Amendment No. 4

version_status_and_amendments.edition_year_of_copy: Third Revision, 1993 (reaffirmed in 2026, incorporating Amendment No. 1, 2, 3, and Amendment No. 4, February 2026)

amendment_slips.description: Substitutes Clause 1 to expand the scope to cover 48 V electric horns, updates terminal testing voltage limits, restricts maximum connecting leads electrical resistance, and replaces legacy IS 9000 environmental test methods with contemporary IS/IEC 60068 standards.

certification_and_marking.certification_status: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under Rule 119 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR), 1989, all electric horns fitted on motor vehicles, agricultural tractors, combine harvesters, and alternate fuel/battery vehicles must conform to IS 1884:1993 and bear the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Manufacturing, importing, or selling non-certified electric horns in India is a punishable statutory offense under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable.

requirements.detail: Every certified horn must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L) legibly engraved or printed on the shell.
Specifies starting, mechanical, electrical, and acoustical limits for electric horns powered by standard direct current electrical systems rated at 6 V, 12 V, 24 V, and 48 V.

To prevent excessive voltage drops and maintain stable sound output, the electrical resistance of the connecting leads (excluding any switch contact in the circuit) must not exceed: a) 0.05 ohm for 6 V; b) 0.10 ohm for 12 V; c) 0.20 ohm for 24 V; and d) 0.40 ohm for 48 V.

requirements.requirement_type: Acoustical Performance and Sound Pressure Limits
requirements.detail: When tested on an open site or in an anechoic chamber at a distance of 2 meters, the sound pressure level (A-weighted) must range between 105 dB(A) and 115 dB(A) for passenger/commercial vehicles (Roots Megasonic: 120 ± 5 dB(A), Uno Minda: 105-110 dB(A)), while remaining within legal RTO and CMVR limits.

During electrical and acoustical evaluations, the test voltage measured directly at the horn terminals must be maintained precisely at: a) 6.5 ± 0.2 V for 6 V horns; b) 13.0 ± 0.3 V for 12 V horns; c) 26.0 ± 0.5 V for 24 V horns; and d) 52.0 ± 1.0 V for 48 V horns.
Every horn must pass updated ingress protection and sealing tests per IS/IEC 60068-2-17 to verify that the solenoid coils and tungsten contact assemblies are fully waterproof.

Prior to mechanical testing, horns must undergo dry heat conditioning in accordance with IS/IEC 60068-2-2 to ensure thermal stability and prevent materials (such as bobbin plastic) from melting under engine bay heat.
Horns must survive extreme sub-zero environment exposures per IS/IEC 60068-2-1 without developing mechanical stiffness, spring fracturing, or sound damping.
The symbols, controls, and indicators associated with the horn must comply with the requirements of IS 15575 (1) and (2).

Electro-mechanical horns must be designed for a minimum endurance mission life of 100,000 cycles (continuous beep-rest intervals) under Indian standards, with modern high-durability variants tested up to 300,000 cycles without structural fatigue or contact wear.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 1884 : 1993 (incorporating Amendment No. 4, February 2026) is the mandatory national Indian Standard specification governing the mechanical, electrical, and acoustical requirements of electric horns for motor vehicles, including two-wheelers, three-wheelers, passenger cars, commercial vehicles, and electric carts. Under India's statutory Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR), all such horns must bear the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) to certify their audio warning effectiveness and high-durability design. The standard regulates standard voltages (6 V, 12 V, 24 V, and 48 V), limits terminal-connection wire resistance, defines precise stroboscopic-type acoustic testing voltages, and enforces strict sound-pressure levels (typically between 105 to 115 decibels) and severe environmental resistance tests (dry heat, cold, and sealing per IS/IEC 60068) alongside a mandatory 100,000-cycle endurance mission life to guarantee continuous road-safety alert performance.
